note: A caller that queues while its listener is away (chapter 15.4 B-39): the listener's pipeline starts on 30 s of backlog that drains in 1 s, then the live sends. The first sample seeds the first epoch on the backlog's oldest; the floor falls with the drain and the first epoch waits for two agreeing buckets (3 s), then moves onto the floor. Until then a PES the seed would put more than lead_max_ns (4 s) ahead is stale and dropped, and its lead stays out of the lead row, so the program never degrades. What left on the seed (the oldest 4 s) and the live content it overlaps once the line moved go as one overlap run per PID, reason backlog, at 3.5-3.7 s: about 30 s per PID; the backlog's oldest 3.5-3.7 s play, 2.5-2.7 s of live content go. Before the fix: degraded (lead) at 5 s, the program 30 s early, then 29 s of live content dropped at the recovery.
